problem: The morning ferry to the island carried only 27 cars. The noon ferry was far busier and carried 46 more cars than the morning one. A seagull rode on the railing the whole way. How many cars did the noon ferry carry?

How many visitors came to the zoo on Sunday afternoon? On Sunday morning just 27 people walked through the gates, and in the afternoon there were 46 more visitors than in the morning. The penguins were fed at lunchtime.
A roller coaster train holds 64 riders, but 81 people are lined up for the next ride. How many people will be left in line once the train is full?
follow_up_questions: While they wait, 29 more people join the line. How many people are in line now?
If everyone in line rides on the following train, how many places on it will be empty?

problem: There are 81 children who want to swim in the first round of the gala, yet the pool only has room for 64. Find how many children must sit out the first round.
follow_up_questions: Before the second round starts, another 29 children sign up. How many children are now waiting for a turn?
All of them swim in the second round. How many places in the pool stay empty?

problem: A delivery van went 68 kilometers to the warehouse before lunch and 85 kilometers to the shops after lunch. What distance did it cover that day?
follow_up_questions: For every 9 kilometers, the van burns one liter of petrol. How many liters did it burn that day?
Each liter of petrol costs 2 dollars. How much did the petrol cost?
The following day the van makes exactly the same trip again. How far did it go over the two days?

problem: How far did the family car travel on Saturday? It went 68 kilometers to Grandma's farm in the morning, then 85 kilometers on to the lake in the evening.
follow_up_questions: The car needs a liter of fuel for each 9 kilometers. How much fuel did it need that day?
Fuel is 2 dollars per liter. What did the family pay for the fuel?
On Sunday they drive the very same distance. Over both days, how many kilometers did the car travel?

problem: A rain barrel in the school garden is full when the water reaches 95 centimeters. At the moment the water is 68 centimeters deep. How many more centimeters of water does the barrel need?
follow_up_questions: Each rainy day adds 9 centimeters of water. How many rainy days will it take to fill it?

problem: How many centimeters taller must the snow fort wall get? The children are aiming for 95 centimeters, and so far it stands at 68 centimeters.
follow_up_questions: Every hour they pack on a layer of snow 9 centimeters thick. How many hours will they need?

problem: Kenji's paper chain is 35 centimeters long. His sister made a chain that is 18 centimeters longer than his. How long is his sister's chain?
follow_up_questions: They join the two chains into one. How long is the joined chain?
A piece 7 centimeters long falls off the joined chain. How long is the chain now?

problem: At the craft table, Priya cut a green ribbon 35 centimeters long; the yellow ribbon she cut next was 18 centimeters longer. What length is the yellow ribbon?
follow_up_questions: She knots the two ribbons end to end. How long is the knotted ribbon?
Then she snips 7 centimeters off it to make a bow. What length is left?

problem: Marta has collected 41 seashells this summer, and her friend Lior has collected 26. How many fewer shells does Lior have than Marta?
By how many points was the Blue team behind? At the end of quiz night the Red team had 41 points, while the Blue team had only 26.
Aunt Rui and Uncle Dev shared the driving on a 70-minute trip to the seaside. Aunt Rui drove for 38 minutes. How many minutes did Uncle Dev drive?
follow_up_questions: Uncle Dev sang one song for every 8 minutes he was driving. How many songs did he sing?

problem: For how long did Tasha's brother read aloud? The two of them took turns during a 70-minute story hour, and Tasha read for 38 minutes.
follow_up_questions: Her brother finished a chapter every 8 minutes. How many chapters did he read?

problem: Mr. Haddad walked into the hardware store with 85 dollars. When he walked out with paint and brushes, he still had 28 dollars. How much money did he spend?
follow_up_questions: The paint cost 39 dollars. How much did the brushes cost?
Each brush was 3 dollars. How many brushes did he buy?
Later he spends half of the money he still has on lunch. How much does lunch cost?

problem: Zainab came home from the school book fair with 28 dollars, though she had set out with 85 dollars. How much had she spent there?
follow_up_questions: She spent 39 dollars on a box set of novels and the rest on bookmarks. How much did the bookmarks cost?
The bookmarks were 3 dollars each. How many bookmarks did she get?
The next day she puts half of the money she came home with into her piggy bank. How much goes into the piggy bank?

problem: Two podcasts are on Neha's playlist: a cooking show that lasts 48 minutes and a science show that lasts 39 minutes. How much shorter is the science show?
follow_up_questions: She plays both shows back to back. How many minutes does that take?

problem: What is the difference in riding time between the two bike routes? The river route takes 48 minutes, while the forest route takes only 39.
follow_up_questions: Gustav rides the river route and then the forest route. How long is he on his bike?

problem: Ramon scored 47 points in a video game. That is 16 points fewer than his cousin Teo scored. How many points did Teo score?
follow_up_questions: What is the total of their two scores?
In the next game Ramon wants to score twice as many points as this time. How many points is that?

problem: Bea has 16 fewer stickers in her album than Ada does. Bea's album holds 47 stickers. Find how many stickers Ada has.
follow_up_questions: How many stickers do the two girls have in all?
By summer Bea hopes to have double the number she has now. How many stickers would that be?

problem: Two garden fences differ in length by 23 meters. The shorter fence is 68 meters long. What is the length of the longer fence?
follow_up_questions: A farmer walks the full length of both fences. How many meters does she walk?

problem: The shorter of the two school corridors is 68 meters long. How long is the other corridor, if it is 23 meters longer?
follow_up_questions: The janitor mops both corridors from end to end. How many meters of corridor does he mop?

problem: The big pot at the soup kitchen already had some soup in it. The cook ladled in 35 cups more, and then the pot held 81 cups. How many cups of soup were in the pot to begin with?
follow_up_questions: Then 27 cups are served at lunch. How many cups of soup are left in the pot?

problem: How many liters of water were in the paddling pool before Dad added more? He poured in 35 liters with the garden hose, and afterwards the pool held 81 liters.
follow_up_questions: The kids splash 27 liters out while playing. How much water is left in the pool?

problem: A science lesson and an art lesson lasted 85 minutes altogether. The science lesson took 47 minutes. How long was the art lesson?
follow_up_questions: There was a 15-minute recess between them. How long was it from the start of science to the end of art?

problem: In the double feature at the drive-in, the first cartoon movie lasted 47 minutes. Both movies together lasted 85 minutes. What was the running time of the second one?
follow_up_questions: Between the films there was a 15-minute snack break. From the start of the first film to the end of the second, how much time passed?

problem: A stack of two boxes in Lena's room is 38 centimeters tall. The bottom box is 21 centimeters tall. How tall is the top box?
follow_up_questions: Lena puts a third box on the stack that is 4 centimeters shorter than the box that was on top. How tall is the stack now?
A toy robot 9 centimeters tall stands on the very top. How many centimeters are left between the robot and a shelf 64 centimeters above the floor?

problem: What is the height of the snowman's head if the whole two-ball snowman is 38 centimeters tall and its body is 21 centimeters tall?
follow_up_questions: Gabi adds a third ball as a hat, 4 centimeters shorter than the head, and sets it on top. How tall is the snowman now?
Then she sticks a twig 9 centimeters long upright on the hat. How many centimeters are left between the twig and a branch hanging 64 centimeters above the ground?

problem: Cycling to the library takes Nora 20 minutes, but her mom's car gets her there in twelve. How many minutes does the car save?
follow_up_questions: Nora gets a ride both ways, there and back, on 5 days. How many minutes does she save altogether?

problem: How much quicker is the train than the bus for Grandpa Sol? The bus takes 20 minutes to reach the market, and the train takes 12 minutes.
follow_up_questions: He takes the train there and back, which is 2 trips a day, for 5 days. How many minutes does he save in all?

problem: Tomás picked 9 strawberries in the garden, and his sister picked 6. A ladybug landed on his basket. How many more strawberries did Tomás pick?
How many more acorns did the red squirrel gather than the grey one? The red squirrel stored 9 acorns, while the grey one stored 6. The wind blew leaves all over the park.
There are 8 children at the art table but only 5 pairs of scissors. If each child needs a pair of scissors, how many children have to wait?
follow_up_questions: The teacher brings 4 more pairs of scissors. How many pairs are left over now?
Later 6 more children join the table. How many children are without scissors then?

problem: Only 5 stalls are ready in the stable, yet 8 horses have arrived, and every horse needs a stall of its own. How many horses have no stall?
follow_up_questions: The farmer builds 4 more stalls. How many stalls are empty now?
Next week 6 new horses come to the stable. How many horses will have no stall then?

problem: Mr. Osei is handing out helmets before the bike lesson. He has 7 helmets, and 11 riders are waiting. How many riders have no helmet?
follow_up_questions: He finds 5 more helmets in the shed. How many helmets are spare now?
After the lesson the helmets are cleaned, 4 at a time. How many batches does that take?
Each batch takes 45 minutes. How many minutes of cleaning is that?

problem: How many campers are left without a sleeping bag? There are 11 campers at the lake, but the counselor has brought only 7 sleeping bags.
follow_up_questions: Then 5 extra sleeping bags turn up in the van. How many sleeping bags are left over?
At the end of the trip all the sleeping bags are packed into big sacks, 4 in each sack. How many sacks are needed?
The camp washer cleans one sack of sleeping bags in 45 minutes. How many minutes does it take to wash them all?

problem: Twelve kids want a turn on the class computers, but there are only 8 computers. How many kids must wait?
follow_up_questions: Each waiting kid gets 5 minutes on a computer. How many minutes do their turns take in all?

problem: At the pottery class, 8 wheels are free and twelve students want to throw a pot. How many students have to wait for a wheel?
follow_up_questions: Every waiting student spends 5 minutes at a wheel. How long do the waiting students' turns last altogether?

problem: By lunchtime 34 trains had arrived at the station and 19 had departed. How many more trains had arrived than departed?
follow_up_questions: In the afternoon 27 more trains departed and none arrived. How many trains departed that day?
Over the whole day, how many more trains departed than arrived?

problem: At the harbor this morning, 19 boats sailed out and 34 boats came in. Find how many more boats came in than sailed out.
follow_up_questions: During the afternoon another 27 boats sailed out, but no boats came in. How many boats sailed out in total that day?
For the full day, by how many did the boats that sailed out outnumber the boats that came in?

problem: On the craft table lie two ribbons: a red one 67 centimeters long and a blue one 39 centimeters long. Both ribbons are made of shiny satin. How much longer is the red ribbon?

How many centimeters taller is the sunflower than the tomato plant? The sunflower in Abebe's garden measures 67 centimeters, and the tomato plant is 39 centimeters tall. His grandmother waters them every evening.
A comic book at the corner store costs 85 cents. Lucía has 48 cents. How many more cents does she need?
follow_up_questions: Her grandfather gives her 4 dimes. How many cents does she have now?

problem: How much more money does Ahmed need for an ice pop that costs 85 cents, if he has only 48 cents in his pocket?
follow_up_questions: His friend lends him 4 dimes. How many cents does he have now?

problem: The library reading challenge has 36 books on its list, and 14 of them are picture books. Hira has finished 29 books from the list. How many books on the list has she not read?
follow_up_questions: Each finished book earns 2 stars, and all of Hira's books count. How many stars did she earn?
Her friend Omar earned 9 stars more than Hira. How many stars did Omar earn?
A gold medal needs 70 stars. How many more stars did Omar need?

problem: Out of the 36 puzzles in his puzzle book, Kenji solved 29. The book also has 14 pages of answers at the back. How many puzzles are still unsolved?
follow_up_questions: He gets 2 points for every puzzle he solved. How many points does he have?
His sister Yumi has 9 points more than Kenji. What is her score?
The puzzle club prize needs 70 points. How many more points does Yumi need?

problem: The flower stall at the market opened with 74 bunches of tulips and closed with 29 bunches. How many bunches were sold?
follow_up_questions: Each bunch sold for 6 dollars. How much money did the stall take in?
The stall had paid 2 dollars for every bunch it sold. How much did it make after paying for those bunches?

problem: How many pies did the bakery sell today? It started the morning with seventy-four pies and had twenty-nine left at closing time.
follow_up_questions: Every pie cost 6 dollars. How much money did the bakery take in for them?
Baking each sold pie had cost the bakery 2 dollars. After those costs, how much money did it make?

problem: A sack of grain at the farm weighed eighteen kilograms. The chickens pecked their way through eleven kilograms of it. How many kilograms were left for the ducks?
follow_up_questions: Another sack with 9 kilograms of grain arrives for the ducks. How much grain do the ducks have now?

problem: What weight of hay is left for the goats? The barn had 18 kilograms of hay, and the cows ate 11 kilograms of it.
follow_up_questions: The farmer brings 9 more kilograms of hay for the goats. How many kilograms of hay do the goats have now?

problem: Two boats are tied up at the dock: a sailboat 12 meters long and a fishing boat 8 meters long. What is the difference in their lengths?
How much longer is the whale model than the shark model at the science center? The whale model stretches 12 meters, and the shark model 8 meters.
The tractor's diesel tank held 82 liters in the morning and 35 liters by evening. How much diesel did the tractor use?
follow_up_questions: Tomorrow the tractor has less field to plow and will need 19 fewer liters than today. How much diesel will it need?
If the farmer does not refill the tank, how many liters will be left at the end of tomorrow?

problem: Find how many liters of water the gardeners used: their big water tank held 82 liters at dawn and 35 liters at dusk.
follow_up_questions: The next day they will need 19 fewer liters than they used today. How much water will they need?
If they start the next day with only the water now in the tank, how many liters will remain at the end of that day?

problem: Jonah had 9 letters to post. The mailbox got full after he had dropped in 6 of them. How many letters were still in his hand?
follow_up_questions: Each of those letters needs 2 stamps, and each stamp costs 5 cents. How many cents will the stamps for them cost?

problem: How many fruit cups were still on Mia's tray? She carried 9 fruit cups to the picnic table and had put down 6 when her brother called her away.
follow_up_questions: Each of the cups left on the tray has 2 scoops of fruit, and each scoop holds 5 grapes. How many grapes are in those cups?

problem: At the park, Lin spent 52 minutes on the climbing frame and 17 minutes on a bench eating a snack. How many more minutes did she spend climbing than sitting?
follow_up_questions: How long did her park visit last in total?
Her mom said she could stay for 90 minutes. How many of those minutes did Lin not use?
Next time she climbs for twice as long. How many minutes is that?

problem: How many more minutes did Kofi practise piano than violin? He played the piano for 52 minutes and the violin for 17 minutes.
follow_up_questions: For how many minutes did he practise altogether?
His teacher asked for 90 minutes of practice. How many minutes short was he?
Tomorrow he will play the piano for double the time. How many minutes will that be?

problem: The pet shop's back room has a 9-kilogram bag of cat food, a 4-kilogram bag of bird seed and a 25-kilogram sack of dog food. How much heavier is the dog food sack than the cat food bag?
follow_up_questions: The shopkeeper scoops 7 kilograms of dog food into smaller bags. Now how much heavier is the dog food sack than the cat food bag?
She also scoops out 3 kilograms of cat food. How many kilograms of dog food and cat food are left in all?

problem: In the garden shed sit a 25-kilogram sack of soil, a 9-kilogram bag of sand and a 4-kilogram bag of pebbles. Find how many more kilograms the soil sack weighs than the sand bag.
follow_up_questions: Grandpa uses 7 kilograms of soil for his pots. By how much does the soil sack outweigh the sand bag now?
He also uses 3 kilograms of sand. How many kilograms of soil and sand are left altogether?

problem: Ms. Ito opened a box of seventy envelopes to send out the school newsletter. After the newsletters were mailed, twenty-three envelopes were still in the box. How many envelopes were used?
follow_up_questions: Each newsletter went in one envelope. If 5 newsletters came back because of wrong addresses, how many families received theirs?

problem: How many paper plates did the picnic use? The pack had 70 plates at the start, and 23 were left over at the end.
follow_up_questions: Every guest used one plate, except that 5 plates were used to cover the salad bowls. How many guests ate at the picnic?

problem: Two sunflowers grow in Ama's yard. The taller one is 96 centimeters, and the shorter one is 38 centimeters. Find how much taller the first sunflower is.
How much longer is the python than the young boa at the reptile house? The python measures 96 centimeters and the young boa 38 centimeters.
In the talent show, the first act lasts only 4 minutes, while the last act lasts 17 minutes. How much longer is the last act?
follow_up_questions: The three acts in between are 9 minutes each. How long is the whole show?
If a 15-minute break is added, how long does the event last?

problem: How many more minutes does Shira spend on the bus than walking to the bus stop? Her walk to the stop takes 4 minutes, and then the bus ride takes 17 minutes.
follow_up_questions: After the bus she rides the train for 3 stops of 9 minutes each. How long is her whole trip?
Counting the 15 minutes she waits on the platform, how long does her journey take?

problem: Arjun scored 7 goals this season and Marta scored 11. How many more goals did Marta score?
follow_up_questions: Next season Arjun hopes to score twice as many goals as this season. How many goals would that be?

problem: Clara grew 11 pumpkins this autumn, but Sam grew just 7. By how many pumpkins did Clara beat Sam?
follow_up_questions: Next year Sam wants to grow double the number he grew this year. How many pumpkins is that?

problem: The small parking lot behind the library has space for nineteen cars, and eleven spaces are already taken. A street sweeper drove past the entrance. How many spaces are still free?
How many hooks are still free on the classroom coat rack? It has 19 hooks, and coats hang on 11 of them. The rack is painted bright yellow.
The sailing club took sixteen boats out on the lake, but four had to come back to shore with torn sails. How many boats were still sailing?
follow_up_questions: Each sailing boat had 5 children on board. How many children were out on the water?
The club fixed 3 of the torn sails and those boats went back out. How many boats are sailing now?

problem: How many of the fair's balloons were still bobbing above the stall? The stall had 16 balloons, but 4 drifted off and got caught in a tree.
follow_up_questions: Each balloon above the stall had 5 stars printed on it. How many stars were there on those balloons?
A worker with a ladder freed 3 of the caught balloons and tied them back on. How many balloons bob above the stall now?

problem: When the chess tournament started, twenty-three parents were watching; by the end, only six were still there. How many parents left before the end?
follow_up_questions: Then 9 more parents arrived to see the final game. How many parents were watching then?
Each parent watching got 2 cookies from the club. How many cookies were handed out?
The club had baked 40 cookies. How many cookies are left?

problem: How many pigeons flew away? There were 23 pigeons in the town square at sunrise, and by noon only 6 were still pecking at crumbs.
follow_up_questions: In the afternoon 9 more pigeons landed. How many pigeons were in the square then?
A lady gave each pigeon 2 bread cubes. How many bread cubes did she give out?
She had 40 bread cubes in her bag. How many are left?

problem: The school photographer printed eighty class photos, and twenty-six were given to families before the assembly. How many photos are still in the folder?
follow_up_questions: After the assembly, 19 more were given out. How many photos are left in the folder?
The leftover photos are put into envelopes of 5 to send to the other classes. How many envelopes are filled?

problem: How many bottles of water are left in the cooler? Race organizers packed 80 bottles and handed 26 to runners during the first hour.
follow_up_questions: In the second hour they handed out 19 more. How many bottles are left in the cooler?
The leftover bottles are packed into crates of 5 for the next race. How many crates is that?

problem: The Ruiz family has had their two dogs for 6 years. Bruno weighs 23 kilograms and Pip weighs 16 kilograms. What is the difference between the dogs' weights?
What is the difference in weight between the two prize pumpkins at the fair? The orange pumpkin weighs 23 kilograms and the white one weighs 16 kilograms. The fair runs for 6 days.
The class fish tank held eighteen liters at the start of the week and seven liters after a leak. How many liters leaked out?
follow_up_questions: The teacher pours in 15 liters of fresh water. How much water is in the tank now?

problem: How much lemonade did the guests drink? The punch bowl at the party had 18 cups of lemonade before the guests came and 7 cups when they left.
follow_up_questions: Then Grandma makes 15 more cups and pours them in. How many cups of lemonade are in the bowl now?

problem: The toy library set out twenty-one board games on its shelf. By Friday only four games were still on the shelf. How many games had been borrowed?
follow_up_questions: On Monday, 6 of the borrowed games were returned to the shelf. How many games are on the shelf now?
How many games are still out with families?
The toy library buys 5 new games. How many games does it own in total now?

problem: How many bikes have been rented out? The bike rental shop lined up 21 bikes in the morning, and by lunchtime only 4 were still in the rack.
follow_up_questions: In the afternoon, 6 of the rented bikes were brought back to the rack. How many bikes are in the rack now?
How many bikes are still out on the roads?
The shop buys 5 brand-new bikes. How many bikes does it have in all now?

problem: The beach shop began the summer with 52 sun hats and ended it with 17. How many sun hats were sold?
follow_up_questions: Each sun hat cost 4 dollars. How much money did the shop take in for them?

problem: How many pairs of mittens did the ski shop sell this winter, if it had fifty-two pairs at the start and seventeen pairs at the end?
follow_up_questions: A pair of mittens costs 4 dollars. How much did the shop earn from mittens?

problem: For the garden project, the class used 6 meters of hose for the herb bed, 31 meters for the vegetable rows and 9 meters for the flower pots. How many more meters of hose went to the vegetable rows than to the herb bed?
follow_up_questions: Hose costs 3 dollars a meter. How much did the hose for the vegetable rows cost?
The herb bed hose was also 3 dollars a meter. How much more did the vegetable hose cost than the herb hose?

problem: How many more meters of blue yarn than yellow yarn did Grandma use? To knit a blanket she used 31 meters of blue yarn, 6 meters of yellow yarn and 9 meters of white yarn.
follow_up_questions: Blue yarn costs 3 dollars a meter. What did Grandma pay for the blue yarn?
The yellow yarn also cost 3 dollars a meter. How much more did she pay for the blue yarn than for the yellow?

problem: This afternoon the ice cream van sold 12 chocolate cones but only 7 lemon cones. The sun was shining all day. How many more chocolate cones were sold?
By how many votes did the dog beat the cat in the class pet vote? The dog got 12 votes and the cat got 7. The vote was held right after lunch.
Selin has swum 9 lengths of the pool, and Bram has swum 7. How many more lengths has Selin swum?
follow_up_questions: One length of the pool is 85 feet. How many more feet has Selin swum than Bram?

problem: How many more laps of the ice rink has Nia skated than Paolo? Nia has done nine laps, and Paolo has done seven.
follow_up_questions: One lap of the rink is 85 meters. How many more meters has Nia skated?

problem: The farm's duck pond had 17 ducks in the morning. After the farmer led some back to the barn, 5 ducks remained on the pond. How many ducks were led back?
follow_up_questions: The ducks led back were shared equally among 4 pens. How many ducks went into each pen?
Later, 2 of those pens were opened and their ducks waddled back to the pond. How many ducks are on the pond now?
Each duck on the pond gets 2 handfuls of grain in the evening. How many handfuls is that?

problem: How many puppies were carried in for their nap? Seventeen puppies were playing in the shelter yard, and after the helpers carried some inside, five were still in the yard.
follow_up_questions: The puppies carried inside were split equally among 4 baskets. How many puppies are in each basket?
After the nap, the puppies from 2 of those baskets were let back into the yard. How many puppies are in the yard now?
Each puppy in the yard gets 2 treats. How many treats are handed out?

problem: A roll of wrapping paper was seventy centimeters long before Mr. Novak cut off twenty-two centimeters for a present. How long is the paper left on the roll?
follow_up_questions: He cuts the rest into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece?

problem: How long is the piece left over after the scout leader cuts 22 centimeters off a 70-centimeter rope for knot practice?
follow_up_questions: She divides the leftover rope into 4 equal lengths for the scouts. How long is each length?

problem: In the gym storeroom, the small medicine ball weighs 3 kilograms, the big one 16 kilograms and the kettlebell 8 kilograms. How much heavier is the big medicine ball than the small one?
follow_up_questions: A cart can carry 40 kilograms. If both medicine balls are put on it, how many more kilograms can it carry?
A 9-kilogram dumbbell is put on the cart too. How many kilograms of space are left?

problem: Find how much more the watermelon weighs than the pineapple. At the fruit stand, a pineapple weighs 3 kilograms, a watermelon 16 kilograms and a bag of oranges 8 kilograms.
follow_up_questions: A shopping trolley can hold 40 kilograms. With the pineapple and the watermelon in it, how many more kilograms could it hold?
A sack of potatoes weighing 9 kilograms goes into the trolley as well. How many more kilograms could it hold now?

problem: A jigsaw puzzle has 92 pieces, and Oskar has already fitted 37 of them. How many pieces still need to be fitted?
How many more steps must the hikers climb? The stairway to the lookout tower has 92 steps, and they have climbed 37 so far.
At the science fair, Kemal's paper rocket flew for nine seconds on its first launch and eleven seconds on its second. How many seconds longer was the second flight?
follow_up_questions: On the third launch it flew three times as long as on the first. How many seconds was that?
How many seconds did the rocket fly in all three launches?

problem: The second time Sami spun his top, it whirled for 11 seconds; the first time it lasted only 9. By how many seconds was the second spin longer?
follow_up_questions: His third spin lasted 3 times as long as the first one. How long was it?
What was the total time of all three spins?

problem: When the train stopped in Milan, 83 travelers got off and 4 stayed on to ride further. How many more travelers got off than stayed on?
follow_up_questions: Then 46 new travelers got on. How many people are on the train now?

problem: On Sunday morning eighty-three guests checked out of the hotel, while four guests stayed on for another night. Find how many more guests checked out than stayed.
follow_up_questions: That afternoon 46 new guests checked in. How many guests are staying at the hotel now?

problem: At the start of the year the art room had 95 blank canvases. Now only 32 are left. How many canvases have been used?
follow_up_questions: The art teacher orders 40 new blank canvases. How many blank canvases does she have now?
If she gives 8 blank canvases to each of 3 classes, how many will be left?

problem: How many sticker sheets have been handed out this term? The school office had ninety-five sheets in January and has thirty-two now.
follow_up_questions: The secretary buys 40 more sheets. How many sheets does the office have now?
If 3 classes each get 8 sheets, how many sheets remain in the office?

problem: The garden fence is 36 meters long, and each rose bush needs 4 meters of room. How many rose bushes can be planted in a row along the fence?
follow_up_questions: The gardener plants 3 such rows. How many rose bushes is that?
Each bush needs 2 liters of water. How many liters are needed for all of them?
The watering can holds 9 liters. How many cans are needed?

problem: How many tents fit in one line along the 36-meter riverbank if every tent needs 4 meters?
follow_up_questions: The campers set up 3 lines like that. How many tents are there?
Each tent sleeps 2 scouts. How many scouts can sleep there?
The scouts are split into patrols of 9. How many patrols are there?

problem: At the end of the first day of the reading contest, the Owls had read 34 books. By the end of the contest they had read 71. How many books did they read after the first day?
follow_up_questions: The Foxes read 8 books fewer than the Owls after the first day. How many books did the Foxes read after the first day?

problem: How many runs did the Hawks add after tea, if they had 34 runs at the tea break and 71 runs at the end of the cricket match?
follow_up_questions: Their rivals made 8 fewer runs than the Hawks after tea. How many runs did the rivals make after tea?

problem: The whale model hanging in the museum is 38 feet longer than the megalodon model, and the whale model measures 92 feet. How long is the megalodon model?
follow_up_questions: If the two models were hung end to end, how long would they be?
The megalodon model is made of sections that are each 18 feet long. How many sections does it have?

problem: The cargo ship is 38 meters longer than the ferry. Find the ferry's length, knowing that the cargo ship measures 92 meters.
follow_up_questions: If both ships were lined up bow to stern, how long would the line be?
The ferry's deck is divided into sections 18 meters long. How many sections are there?

problem: Before the school book sale, the class money box held 19 dollars. When the last book was sold, the box held 64 dollars. How much money did the book sale bring in?
follow_up_questions: The class then took 28 dollars out to pay for new paints. How much is in the box now?
The next week the class sells 12 more books for 3 dollars each and puts that money in the box. How much is in the box after that?
A class rug costs 90 dollars. How much more must go into the box before the class can buy it?

A local shop then gives 25 dollars. Once the 80 dollar sports balls are paid for, how much money is left over?

problem: What did the two clubs collect in total for the animal shelter, if the chess club gave 27 dollars and the drama club gave 34 dollars?
follow_up_questions: The shelter needs 80 dollars for a new dog kennel. How much more money is needed?
A vet then donates 25 dollars. After the 80 dollar kennel is bought, how much money is left?

problem: Ayumi has 32 flowers to tie into bouquets of 4 for the wedding tables. How many bouquets can she make?
How many teams of 4 can the coach make from 32 players?
The scouts' car wash took in 18 dollars on Saturday and 25 dollars on Sunday. How much did it take in over the weekend?
follow_up_questions: Soap and sponges cost 15 dollars. How much profit did the scouts make?
They spend the profit on flashlights at 4 dollars each. How many flashlights can they buy?

problem: How much money did the lemonade stand earn in two days, if it made 18 dollars on Friday and 25 dollars on Saturday?
follow_up_questions: Lemons and cups cost 15 dollars. What was the profit?
The children spend the profit on movie tickets that cost 4 dollars each. How many tickets can they buy?

problem: A tour boat captain makes 3 trips around the bay each day, with 5 passengers on every trip. How many passengers does he take out in a day?
follow_up_questions: Each passenger pays 8 dollars per trip. How much does the captain earn in one day?
He spends 35 dollars a day on fuel. How much does he keep?
How much does he keep over 4 days like this?

problem: How many students does a tennis coach teach in a day if she gives 3 lessons, each with 5 students?
follow_up_questions: Every student pays 8 dollars for a lesson. What does she earn in one day?
Court rental costs her 35 dollars each day. How much money does she keep?
What does she keep after 4 days of lessons like this?

problem: Pizza and drinks for the class party cost 52 dollars together. The pizza alone cost 35 dollars. What did the drinks cost?
How much did the hats cost, if the gloves and hats Dad bought came to 52 dollars and the gloves cost 35 dollars?
The pizza shop handed out 40 vouchers, and 27 of them were brought back and used. How many vouchers were never used?
follow_up_questions: Each used voucher saved the customer 3 dollars. How much did customers save in total?
Printing cost the shop 2 dollars for every voucher it handed out. What did the printing cost?
How much more did customers save than the shop paid for printing?

problem: Only 27 of the 40 free swim passes the pool gave away were ever used. How many passes were never used?
follow_up_questions: Each pass that was used saved a swimmer 3 dollars. What was the total saving?
Making the passes cost the pool 2 dollars each, for every pass it gave away. What did making the passes cost?
By how much were the swimmers' savings bigger than the pool's cost?

problem: Chloe is saving for a telescope. She puts 6 dollars into her jar every week. How much will she have after 8 weeks?
follow_up_questions: The telescope costs 60 dollars. How many more dollars will she need?
How many more weeks of saving is that?

problem: How much money will Mateo have saved for his soccer boots after 8 weeks if he saves 6 dollars a week?
follow_up_questions: The boots cost 60 dollars. How much more does he need to save?
How many more weeks must he save to reach that amount?

problem: Nadia bought 20 bags of potting soil for the school garden and used 13 of them in April. Worms wriggled in every pot. How many bags has she not used yet?
How many puzzles are still in their boxes? Jakob got 20 puzzles for his birthday and has finished 13 of them. His favourite shows a lighthouse.
In the farm's chicken coop there are 14 brown hens and 9 speckled ones. How many hens live in the coop?
follow_up_questions: On Saturday 6 hens are sold to a neighbor. How many are left in the coop?
Each remaining hen eats 2 scoops of grain a day. How many scoops does the farm need each day?

problem: How many kittens are at the animal shelter if there are 14 grey kittens and 9 black kittens?
follow_up_questions: On Saturday 6 kittens are adopted. How many kittens are left?
Every kitten left gets 2 small meals a day. How many meals does the shelter serve each day?

problem: Hanna's piggy bank held 28 dollars, and her aunt slipped in another 15 dollars for the ski trip. How much money is in the piggy bank now?
follow_up_questions: The ski trip costs 35 dollars. How much will Hanna have after paying for it?

problem: How much money does Omar have for the zoo trip? He had saved 28 dollars, and his mom added 15 dollars.
follow_up_questions: The zoo trip costs 35 dollars. After paying, how much money will Omar have left?

problem: The dance class is learning 6 new dances this term, and each dance has 4 parts. How many parts will the class learn?
follow_up_questions: They have already learned 9 parts. How many are still to learn?

problem: How many pages must Wen read for book club if there are 6 short stories with 4 pages each?
follow_up_questions: Wen has read 9 pages already. How many pages are left?

problem: A shipment of 72 toy cars arrives at the toy shop, and the staff pack them into boxes of 8. How many boxes do they use?
follow_up_questions: Each toy car sells for 6 dollars. How much money comes in if one full box is sold?
How much would the shop take in if every toy car were sold?

problem: How many crates does the farmer need for 72 melons if each crate holds 8 melons?
follow_up_questions: Every melon sells for 6 dollars. What is one full crate worth?
What would all the melons bring in together?

problem: Each of the 9 players on the team got a 4 dollar medal at the end of the season. What did the medals cost the coach?
What did Mrs. Popescu spend on party hats if she bought one for each of the 9 guests and each hat cost 4 dollars?
The gardener paid each helper 8 dollars for the afternoon, and she paid 56 dollars in total. The weeds were piled up by the compost bin. How many helpers were there?
follow_up_questions: Next week she hires 3 more helpers at the same pay. How much will she pay out then?

problem: How many tickets did the class buy for the puppet show, if they paid 56 dollars and each ticket was 8 dollars? The theater curtain was dark red.
follow_up_questions: For the next show, 3 extra children come along, each needing a ticket at the same price. What will all the tickets cost then?

problem: Ngozi had 17 dollars when she got to the zoo gift shop. She spent 9 dollars on a toy giraffe. How much money does she have left?
follow_up_questions: She uses the rest to buy postcards at 2 dollars each. How many postcards can she buy?

problem: How much money did Lukas have left after paying 9 dollars for a sandwich, if he started with 17 dollars?
follow_up_questions: With what is left he buys apples at 2 dollars each. How many apples can he buy?

problem: Ana's swimming course has 12 lessons. She has gone to 7 so far. How many lessons are left?
follow_up_questions: Each lesson costs 6 dollars. What will the rest of the lessons cost?
Ana has 21 dollars saved. How much more does she need?

problem: How many chapters are left for the class to read? Their novel has 12 chapters, and they have finished 7.
follow_up_questions: The teacher writes 6 questions for each remaining chapter. How many questions is that?
The class has already answered 21 of them. How many questions are still to do?

problem: A packet of trading cards has 8 cards. Rafael opens 7 packets. How many cards does he have?
follow_up_questions: He sells the cards to friends in sets of 4 at 3 dollars a set. How much will he make if he sells them all?

problem: How many muffins come out of the oven if the baker bakes 7 trays with 8 muffins on each tray?
follow_up_questions: She sells them in boxes of 4 for 3 dollars a box. How much money does she make if every box sells?

problem: The cable car carries 8 skiers on every trip up the mountain. How many skiers does it carry in 9 trips?
follow_up_questions: Each skier pays 5 dollars for the ride. How much does the cable car collect?
Electricity for those trips costs 60 dollars. How much is left after paying for it?
The owner splits what is left equally among her 3 workers. How much does each worker get?

problem: How many passengers does the sightseeing bus carry on 9 tours if each tour carries 8 passengers?
follow_up_questions: Every passenger pays 5 dollars. How much money does the bus company take in?
The fuel for the day costs 60 dollars. How much money is left once that is paid?
What is left is shared equally by 3 tour guides. How much does each guide get?

problem: Amina's lunch at the museum cafe came to 13 dollars, and she paid with a 20-dollar bill. How much change did she get?
follow_up_questions: In the gift shop she spent 4 dollars of her change on a pencil. How much of her change was left?

problem: What change does Jorge get from a 20 dollar note when he pays for a 13 dollar haircut?
follow_up_questions: He drops 4 dollars of the change into the tip jar. How much of his change does he keep?

problem: After the egg hunt, the children had found 42 chocolate eggs. They shared them evenly among 6 baskets. How many eggs went into each basket?
follow_up_questions: From every basket, the children ate all but 2 of the eggs. How many eggs were eaten from each basket?
Counting all 6 baskets, how many eggs were eaten?

problem: How many water balloons did each team get, if 42 water balloons were split evenly between 6 teams at the summer fair?
follow_up_questions: Every team threw all but 2 of its balloons. How many did each team throw?
How many balloons did all 6 teams throw altogether?

problem: The drama club already knew 9 songs for its musical. During the last weeks of practice the members learned 6 more. How many songs do they know now?
follow_up_questions: On show night there was only time for 8 of them. How many songs were left out?

problem: How many card tricks can Ilya do now? He knew 9 tricks before the holidays and learned 6 new ones during them.
follow_up_questions: At the talent show he has time for 8 tricks. How many tricks does he leave out?

problem: Seven neighbors had their dogs washed at the scouts' dog wash, and each paid 8 dollars. How much did the scouts collect from them?
follow_up_questions: Shampoo and towels had cost 19 dollars. How much money is left after paying for those?
In the afternoon more dog owners brought in another 24 dollars. How much do the scouts have now?
Their camping trip costs 90 dollars. How much more do they need to raise?

problem: How much did the class make from the 7 families who bought a pie at the bake sale, if each pie cost 8 dollars?
follow_up_questions: Flour and fruit for the pies cost 19 dollars. How much is left once those are paid for?
Later, cookie sales add 24 dollars. How much does the class have now?
The class wants 90 dollars for a museum visit. How much more must it raise?

problem: Over the summer Kaito helped younger kids learn to swim. He charged 5 dollars a lesson and earned 35 dollars. How many lessons did he give?
follow_up_questions: Each lesson lasted 20 minutes. How many minutes did he teach in all?
He had hoped to give 10 lessons. How many lessons short did he fall?

problem: How many paintings did Sofia sell at the street fair, if each painting cost 5 dollars and she earned 35 dollars?
follow_up_questions: Each painting took her 20 minutes to paint. How many minutes did the sold paintings take her?
She had hoped to sell 10 paintings. How many fewer did she sell?

problem: On Saturday the museum's donation box collected 18 dollars in the morning and 23 dollars in the afternoon. The box is made of clear glass. How much was in the box at closing time?
follow_up_questions: The next day the staff used 15 dollars of it for new brochures. How much was left in the box?

problem: How much money was in the band's busking hat at the end of the day? They collected 18 dollars before lunch and 23 dollars after lunch. The drummer wore sunglasses all day.
follow_up_questions: That evening they spent 15 dollars on pizza. How much money is left?

problem: On Sunday Dad baked 64 muffins and packed them equally into 8 lunch tins, one tin for each school lunch he had planned. How many muffins went into each tin?
follow_up_questions: Each tin is used for one lunch. After 5 lunches, how many muffins are still left in the tins?

problem: How many crackers go in each snack bag, if Grandpa splits 64 crackers equally into 8 bags for the camping trip, one bag per hike?
follow_up_questions: One bag is eaten on each hike. After 5 hikes, how many crackers are left?

problem: On Saturday the juice bar sold 27 orange smoothies and 35 berry smoothies. What was the total number of smoothies sold that day?
follow_up_questions: Sunday's sales were 9 smoothies fewer than Saturday's. How many smoothies were sold on Sunday?

problem: How many hot dogs did the stand at the stadium sell on Friday, if it sold 27 with mustard and 35 with ketchup?
follow_up_questions: On Saturday it sold 9 fewer hot dogs than on Friday. How many did it sell on Saturday?

problem: For Sunday's circus show, 38 children's tickets and 25 adult tickets were sold. How many tickets were sold in all?
follow_up_questions: The tent has 80 seats. How many seats were empty?

problem: How many people rode the steam train on its first trip, if 38 children and 25 grown-ups were on board?
follow_up_questions: The train has 80 seats. How many seats were not taken?

problem: The school is putting new cushions on its benches. Each of the 6 benches needs 8 cushions. How many cushions should be ordered?
follow_up_questions: Cushions come in packs of 12. How many packs are needed?
Each pack costs 15 dollars. What will the packs cost?

problem: How many plants does the gardener need for 6 flower beds, with 8 plants in each bed?
follow_up_questions: The plants are sold in trays of 12. How many trays should she buy?
A tray costs 15 dollars. What is the cost of the trays?

problem: The library ordered 5 boxes of bookmarks for its reading fair, with 8 bookmarks in each box. The bookmarks have a picture of an owl. How many bookmarks arrived?
follow_up_questions: Librarians handed out 33 bookmarks on the first morning. How many were left over?

problem: How many hot dog buns did the picnic team get? They bought 5 packs with 8 buns in each pack. The packs were stored in a cool box.
follow_up_questions: The guests ate 33 buns at lunch. How many buns were left?

problem: Each of the 9 players at basketball practice took 6 free throws. Work out how many free throws were taken.
How many paper cranes did the class fold, if 9 children each folded 6 cranes?
Five skaters were already on the frozen pond when the ice was declared safe. By noon 8 more had come with their skates. How many skaters were on the pond then?
follow_up_questions: In the afternoon 6 of them went home for hot chocolate. How many stayed on the ice?
Each skater who stayed did 4 more laps before dark. How many laps was that in all?

problem: How many swimmers were in the lake by noon? There were 5 swimmers there at sunrise, and 8 more jumped in later in the morning.
follow_up_questions: Then 6 of them got out to dry off. How many swimmers are still in the lake?
Each one still in the water swims out to the raft 4 more times. How many trips to the raft is that altogether?
